fact_check.claim: Access Fund applications open Sept 21, 2026 through April 15, 2027; reviewed rolling on the 15th of each month
fact_check.note: Page gives the same window and the 15th-of-month rolling review.

fact_check.claim: Each Access Fund category needs its own application
Basic Needs provides a cold weather coat, hat and gloves through the Cornell Store
The Store emails approved applicants and you pick items up there
fact_check.note: Fetched page says decisions go to your Cornell email and items are provided through the Cornell Store; the Store-emails-and-pickup detail was not in what I got back.

fact_check.claim: Maximize Cornell: temporary laptop and cell phone replacement, career readiness attire, graduation expenses, gym memberships for first-semester students only
Power of Experience pays up to $1,500 and asks for a resume, a budget and an alternative plan

Undergraduates attach their 2026-27 Financial Aid Summary; fund is not an emergency fund; eligibility is full-time undergraduate, graduate and professional students on the Ithaca campus with low or limited income and high need
FGLI office in Barnes Hall Room 200, 607-254-1288, FGLIEmpowerment@cornell.edu
Big Red Basics: free hygiene cabinet in 206 Willard Straight Hall, Mon-Fri 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., no request or appointment
Swipe Out Hunger fall 2026 runs September 21 to December 8; FGLI office is contact for urgent food needs
Winter break housing $125 per one-week option, $500 full break; application opens Oct 1, due Dec 1; must be returning to on-campus housing for spring
fact_check.note: Matches. Page itself warns its text is garbled, as the article says.

fact_check.claim: Students outside a designated open building can apply only for the full break at $500, in limited flex spaces
HILC/Low Rise 8 and Loving House residents stay free; Veterans House residents stay free because it is in the academic-year license
fact_check.note: Free stay confirmed for all three.

fact_check.claim: HILC/Low Rise 8 and Loving House free stay is 'funded by individual gifts'
fact_check.note: The gifts funding did not appear in the page content I retrieved (only 'no additional cost'). Drop the clause or confirm.

fact_check.claim: Fall meal plans end with the semester
Cornell Dining closed Dec 25, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027; fall BRBs work at open cafés through Dec 24 and Jan 4 to 19; City Bucks for off-campus meals or groceries
Books and course materials $1,234 and personal expenses $2,182 (annual, not billed)
Transportation listed as 'Varies', costs to and from campus vary by region
Student Health Plan not in estimate; fees not charged to all students are not eligible for need-based grant or scholarship aid; may request loan funding
2025-26 Student Health Plan $3,685 new / $4,020 returning; waiver due July 31
fact_check.note: Matches the Sun. Prior-year price from a newspaper, flagged in the article as needing a current check; acceptable but an official source is better.

fact_check.claim: Michelle Van-Ess Grant, senior associate dean of students, said books, travel, professional clothing and basic needs weigh on first-gen and low-income students
FirstGen Forward summary of uAspire: indirect expenses are more than half the cost of college and colleges often do not tell students
fact_check.note: Page says 'more than half the cost of college, yet colleges fail to give students essential information'. 'Often' is a slight softening, acceptable.

fact_check.claim: 2021 Sun: aid packages do not adjust for international flights; some students go years between visits home; work-study capped at $1,300 per semester
fact_check.note: All three supported; article dated and flagged as possibly outdated.

fact_check.claim: Rafael Bitanga '23 quoted saying resources still feel limited in times of need; guide planned sections on employment, scholarships, housing, textbooks, clothing, food, study abroad
fact_check.note: Quote: 'it still feels limited during the times of need, especially in emergencies'; paraphrase is fair.

fact_check.claim: In a 2018 Chronicle piece, Shakima Clency, director of FGLI student support, is described as working on strain such as students who cannot go home over breaks or worry about food when dining hours shrink
fact_check.note: The Chronicle says low-income students may not be able to go home over breaks or may worry about food when dining hours shrink, as a general challenge. It does not say Clency is working on that strain; it describes her as coordinating partnerships and 'wrap-around support'. The attribution overstates the source.

beats_top.query: cornell first-gen low income hidden costs
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2018 Chronicle feature on the first-gen experience with no cost list, prices, deadlines or office contacts; our page gives the specific gaps, current dates and fees, and the Access Fund path for each.
changes: Fix the Clency attribution so the one Chronicle reference matches what it says.
Remove or source the 'funded by individual gifts' clause.

fixes: In the Breaks section, change the sentence 'In a 2018 Chronicle piece, Shakima Clency, director of first-generation and low-income student support, is described as working on strain such as students who cannot go home over breaks or worry about food when dining hours shrink' to say only what the source says, e.g. 'A 2018 Cornell Chronicle feature notes that low-income students may not be able to go home over breaks or may worry about food when dining hours shrink.' In 'Winter clothing', soften 'The Store emails approved applicants, and you pick the items up there' to 'Decisions go to your Cornell email, and the items are provided through the Cornell Store', which matches the Access Fund page; source https://scl.cornell.edu/sub/belonging-support-services/centers-student-equity-empowerment-and-belonging/first-generation-low-income-student-support/access-fund
